4th Period.workingNow: Listening for arrow key presses and changing the direction your snake travels.
4th Period.weeklyDeliverable: week04-snake.html — a working Snake game in JavaScript, linked from your index page and pushed to GitHub Pages by Sunday night.
4th Period.smartGoal: I can listen for a key press and change a direction variable so that I can steer my snake with the arrow keys.
4th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.12 — Design and iteratively develop programs that combine control structures, including nested loops and compound conditionals.
4th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.1 — Exchanging information and ideas with others through collaborative discussions.
agenda: I do: key listener + direction variables (12 min)
We do: wire up left and right together (8 min)
You do: add up and down, test all four (20 min)
Check yourself: hard refresh, steer it, push (5 min)
4th Period.connections: Yesterday your square moved, but only one direction, forever. Today you add a listener that watches the keyboard and changes direction. Tomorrow it gets a body, an apple, and a way to lose.

6th Period.workingNow: Building the Grow Box: a draw loop plus one variable that follows your mouse.
6th Period.weeklyDeliverable: Game Lab Lessons 2 and 3 complete, plus your Grow Box program — a shape that changes size when you move the mouse — shared with Ms. Herrick by Sunday night.
6th Period.smartGoal: I can put my shape inside a draw loop so that it redraws over and over and can change while the program is running.
6th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.12 — Design and iteratively develop programs that combine control structures, including nested loops and compound conditionals.
6th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.5 — Listening actively to spoken English in a range of social and academic contexts.
agenda: Quick overview: today's plan + handout (3 min)
I do: the draw loop — code that runs forever (10 min)
We do: build the base Grow Box together (10 min)
You do: your own Grow Box, Level 1 (20 min)
Exit Ticket: does your square react to the mouse? (5 min)
6th Period.connections: Every program you have written so far ran once, top to bottom, and stopped. Today you meet the draw loop — the pattern underneath every game ever made — and your square finally changes while the program is running. Tomorrow you add your own level and share it.
